message: player_4, I didn't visit you last night — I held my action. Whatever you followed, it wasn't me coming to your door. If your follow result really said player_3 visited player_4, then either you're misreporting it or you're making it up; show me the exact wording before I believe it.

player_3, nobody in this cast visits players as a passive act. If you didn't visit player_4, then either player_4 fabricated the result or you're refusing to name your role. Name the role you hold and I'll judge the two of you against player_2, player_9 and player_10, who've said nothing.

We lost the healer and the sentinel on night one, so the town is behind and I don't want to burn the day on nothing. Concretely: player_6 was the sentinel and died to the SK, so whatever they did night 1 was a watch — the fact they were visiting player_7 tells us someone trusted or wanted to check player_7, not that player_7 is guilty. I'd rather pressure someone with a claim to make than vote blind; who's got a night result they're willing to state?

player_4, your story doesn't work: a follow tells you where player_3 went, not who came to your door. You can't learn \"player_3 visited player_4\" from a follow — that phrasing is what a watch on you would say. So either you watched yourself (no such result) or the claim's made up. Which is it?

player_4, one missing piece: the real Trailseer is still in this game and only has to say 'player_4 is lying' to end you. Nobody has. player_3, your Sentinel result doesn't prove you're the Sentinel — but player_4's follow is the weaker claim: if it were true, a wolf would be caught on night 1, which a real Trailseer would happily confirm. I'd vote player_4 today.

I've got something concrete: player_6, our sentinel, targeted player_7 on night 1 before dying. Sentinels watch; they don't attack. So player_7, what did you get up to that made the sentinel look at you — did anyone target you last night? That's the one lead we have, and I'd rather chase it than guess at quiet people.

player_3, I'm not disputing your watch — you're right that I visited player_7 on night 2, that's my track. On night 3 my track showed player_7 targeting no one, and player_5 died that night. So player_7 either held the check or is lying about making it; they should say which.

I like this test, actually. Player_4 says I visited them; a night action that isn't a kill on them is just a visit. I'd rather answer with a proposal: if I get checked by player_5 tonight, do I come up clean? That gives us something testable instead of a he-said.

Since I claimed trailseer, here's a real result I can test against your claims: night 2 I tracked player_9, and they targeted player_4 — the chanteuse who died struck by a sigil. That sure looks like player_9 was the sigilist, not an investigator. So player_9's 'investigator' claim was a bluff. Worth knowing before we trust anything else they said.

Yesterday's vote is the cleanest lead we have: player_7 and player_8 both tried to swing the lynch onto player_4, who turned out to be the chanteuse. Wolves don't bus a packmate without reason — that redirect smells like one of them trying to save her. I also followed player_9 last night and saw them at player_4's door, which fits a real role visiting, so 9's death doesn't clear the 7/8 pair for me at all. I'd vote player_8 or player_7 today; which of you wants to explain that vote?

player_4, your own two sentences don't match: first it was \"player_3 came to visit me,\" then it was \"player_3 visited player_4.\" A follow doesn't put a name at your door — it puts the followed player out at someone else's door. One of those phrasings is you describing a watch, so which ability do you actually hold? And player_7's right that the wording is the tell, so don't paper over it.

player_4, I'll answer you straight: I pushed player_7 because the pack's kill vanished without a word from the Game Master. No attack announced means the target couldn't die that night, and on night 1 only the Necromancer can't die — so the bite went into player_7 and we never heard about it. Your follow dispute doesn't change that player_7 is a lone killer sitting safe, and I'd spend the vote there rather than on misremembered wording.

I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they went to player_3, who died to the wolves. The GM's own lines rule player_1 out as Necromancer or Speculator, so that visit lines up with being the wolf who carried the kill (Chanteuse), or at best a town role that should just say which one. What did you go to player_3 for, player_1?

player_3, I'm not disputing your watch on me — I did visit player_7 on night 2, that's my follow, so that line checks out. The question is player_7: I watched them target player_8 on night 2, but last night they targeted no one, which contradicts the night-3 check on player_5 they'd announced. If I'm lying about that, where's player_5's check result?

Yes, I came to player_7 on night 2 — that was my follow, the same one I'm using to say they stayed home last night. Last night I followed player_7 again and got no visit, so either their check never happened or they were blocked and should say so. Which is it?

One thing worth pinning before we vote: player_3, your version has you watching player_4's door AND never visiting anyone. A Sentinel watch is a visit to the player watched — so which is it, did you sit outside player_4's door or not? And player_10's \"the kill must have hit the Necromancer\" is not the only reading; a held, blocked, or protected swing looks the same from outside.

A held action isn't a contradiction under these rules — player_7 announcing a plan and then holding is legal, so that's not the lie to chase. Here's what bugged me: everyone kept saying player_7 was attacked, but the only confirmed save is night 2, and no wolf went to player_7 on night 3. So on night 3, the one night we have no sighting from either of you, who did the last wolf go for? Neither of you can show a night-3 read. player_6 has said nothing and abstained twice — that's where I'd start today.

A fact nobody's mentioned: player_8 can't be the Illusionist. I'm the Investigator and I checked player_8 night 1 — Not suspicious — so my result rules out every wolf for him, not just one. That means the living wolf is among player_2, player_3, player_4, player_6, player_7, player_9, player_10, and today's fight over follow-vs-watch wording may be a genuine misunderstanding: player_3's Sentinel watch wouldn't appear in his own watch, so player_4's follow could still be real. I'd not hang a lynch on that dispute.

player_4, here's the thing you keep skipping: I'm the one with a result on you, and it says nobody targeted you last night — and since you're alive and unannounced, nothing that touched you could have been hidden. So 'player_3 visited player_4' isn't a wording slip, it's a result that can't exist. Where did it come from?

Since the table is arguing over claims, here's a check I can stand behind: I checked player_8 last night and got Not suspicious. That doesn't make them the Sigilist, but it rules out player_8 being the wolf, so the last wolf is one of player_3, player_4, player_6, player_7, player_9, player_10, or player_2. One of player_3/player_4 is lying flat-out — I'd rather the vote land there than on a quiet player we can't test, and I'm saving my last check for whichever of them survives the day.

Out of checks since night 2, so last night I did nothing - that's why you saw nothing, and it tells you exactly nothing about me. The thing that does matter: player_8 claimed I checked them night 1 with a clean read, and I never checked them until night 2. One of us is lying there, and player_8 should be the one answering for it.

player_3, thanks for the direct answer — yes, I did visit player_7 on night 2, so that part of your watch is real to me. But night 3 I followed player_7 and saw nothing, so their 'check on player_5' never happened, or they got roleblocked. player_7, which is it?

Player_6 was the sentinel, and I tracked them last night — they targeted player_7. That's a fact you can all test against whatever player_7 says they did. A sentinel visiting someone on night 1 is worth explaining, so player_7, what's your story?",

player_1, a sigil is spent when it's placed whether or not it triggers, and you reportedly placed one on player_3 on night 4 — so where did your other sigil go? Two sigils, one game, and you've only ever named one use; I want the night it was spent and on whom, because that's the part that has to line up.

One thing nobody's flagged: player_8's sigil story only works if player_1 actually attacked someone on night 1 — a sigil only triggers on an attacker. Yet no attack on night 1 was announced at all. So either the attack hit the one player night-immune on night 1, or the sigilist claim is off. That's worth pinning down before we trust player_8.

Fine, player_3, no fight there — I was on player_7 night 2, so your watch checks out. The result I'm standing on is night 3: I followed player_7 and they targeted nobody, so the announced check on player_5 never happened. Player_7, what were you actually doing that night, and why claim a check you didn't make?

player_1, I'm the Sigilist — I've held both sigils unused all game, which I'll say outright since you're claiming my role. A real Sigilist with sigils spent would be able to name who they placed them on; you just said your night-4 sigil 'had no effect,' which is exactly what a wolf who visited the night's victim wants to say. If you were the Sigilist, why hide it until now while a healer and sentinel died revealed?

Yes, that was me on night 2 — I followed player_7 and saw them go to player_8. Last night I followed player_7 again and got nothing, so the check on player_5 that they announced on day 3 never happened. Player_7, you said the last check goes on player_5; why did you stay home instead?

Fresh info to get the day moving: I followed player_6 last night and saw them visit player_7 — so the sentinel was watching someone, which tells us player_7 drew attention but not much else. Two deaths on night 1 means we need claims today; anyone who saw a visit, or was visited by someone unexpected, should say so before we vote, since that's the only way to catch the killer's trail.

My track on player_9 lines up with their claim — they targeted player_4 last night, which fits a check. So I'm treating player_9's investigator claim as probably real, and that leaves both hostiles (illusionist and serial killer) among you four: player_1, player_5, player_7, player_8.

The real tell in the player_3/player_4 thing isn't follow vs watch — it's that player_4 says his result literally named player_3 as a visitor to himself. A follow on player_3 shows where player_3 went, so it would say \"player_3 visited player_6\" or whoever, not player_4. He's quoting a watch result and calling it a follow. Player_4, which role is it and what's the exact wording?

One thing nobody's pressed: player_7 was attacked on night 2, so a wolf came to them that night — player_3, if you really watched player_7, that wolf visit should have been in your list. Your report only had player_2, player_5 and player_10. So what exactly did your watch return, and does it match a real save?

Your reasoning has a gap: the wolves' kill n1 not landing doesn't mean it hit the Necromancer — the target could've been the player the healer saved, or just a held pack if they hit someone immune for another reason. Pointing at me is a guess dressed as deduction, and it lets player_3/player_4's contradiction go unexamined. If the pack's target were really the Necromancer, the wolves already know who it is and would be pushing elsewhere — so why does the loudest push come from you?

We're three left and both wolves are gone, so the Necromancer is either player_6 or player_8. I followed player_6 last night and they visited no one. That's not proof either way, it fits both a hold and a Necromancer standing pat. player_6, what have you done nights 1-5 and where do you stand on player_8's sigil claim?

I'm the Trailseer. Last night I followed player_1 and saw them visit player_3 — that's the night player_3 got killed by the wolves. Since only the wolf carrier visits for the kill, player_1 has to explain that visit. A protection or a wolf kill, what was it?

Here's the wrinkle the 3-vs-4 fight hides: there was no wolf kill announced night 1, so the pack's target survived because it was the Necromancer. That target knows they were hit. Player_3, if you really sat a watch on player_4, you'd have seen the wolves' carrier visit whoever got bitten — so state who targeted whom besides me. And player_4: a follower sees only a destination, so how do you know your result wasn't the Sentinel's own watch trail?

Someone moved on me last night. player_3, I tracked you on night 1 and you targeted me. That's not a death sentence — you could have been the healer saving me — but nothing was attacked last night except player_1, so I want to hear what you actually did and why me. If you claim healer, that's checkable later by who shows up saved.

I didn't visit you, player_4. I stayed on my own action last night and made no visit at your door, so your follow is wrong or invented. Note the chanteuse is dead, so nobody was blocked night 1 — if your follow really saw a visitor to player_4, name who it showed, because 'player_3' can't be true from my side.

One thing worth nailing down today: player_8 says player_7 checked them night 1, player_7 says night 2. Two players can't both be right about the night. player_8, what exactly did player_7's result on you say, and when? A real Investigator output is specific enough that a fake account usually cracks there.

Worth noting on the player_4/player_3 spat: player_4 initially said 'player_3 came to visit me', which is a watch's wording, then corrected to a follow reading. That switch is the tell — a trailseer would have said 'went to' the first time. I'd like player_4 to give his exact wording unprompted before we weigh player_3's denial.

I'm the trailseer, and I have a result worth putting out now that we're down to four. Last night I followed player_1 and watched them go to player_3 — the sentinel who died that same night. player_1 can't be the Necromancer or the Speculator, so what were they doing at player_3's door?

player_7, you said the last check went on player_5 last night. Did you actually go to them, or did something stop you? I have a specific reason to ask: I have a sighting that says you went nowhere last night, so if the check happened I'd like to hear how.

Here's something concrete: I'm the Sentinel, and I watched player_7 on night 2. My watch shows player_2, player_5 and player_10 all came to player_7 — the night the wolves attacked them. player_5 was the healer who saved them, and player_2 was the Illusionist wolf. So player_10 needs to explain that visit, because the only town roles that visit at night are limited and I've now got you on the record at the door of a wolf-attacked player.

Everyone's stuck on player_7 vs player_10, but their accounts actually line up on night 2, so that argument isn't going to crack anything. The real gap: player_5 died with a full will and nobody has tested the healer logic against player_7's save. If player_7 is the Investigator, who did they read besides player_8? That's an untested result lying around. I'd rather see player_7 or player_10 say which living name they can still testify against than watch them relitigate night 3.

Careful, love — if player_3 watched your door and your follow saw him go to it, those two fit perfectly, so the only thing left is what he did there. But here's the sharper point: the wolves' kill on night 1 hit someone who couldn't die, and the only such body is the Necromancer. That's a real hole, and it's not player_3 or you. I'd look at who's coasting on this noise.

Straight answer, player_4: no follow was needed to disprove you. I did visit no one on night 1 — but more to the point, a follow on me would have shown my destination, and you said \"player_3 visited player_4,\" meaning your own door. You don't get that wording from a follow on me. So which ability, on which target, actually produced that result?

Two things stand out to me. First, player_4's \"result\" is phrased as a follow but reads like a watch on their own door — a Trailseer tracks where someone went, a Sentinel sees who came to a target, so exactly one of those two claims is the truth and one is a fudge. Second, player_8's sigil story matches the morning report precisely, including that player_1 carried the kill, which is a strong detail to invent — I lean believing it.
